evidence: A Godot 4.5 prototype for authoring reusable 12 fps stepped animation poses against a skeleton profile. The visible authoring rig is now 3D-only.
- Loads the Ironhelm Biped skeleton profile generated from the downloaded GLB archive.
- Displays a 3D stick rig and always-on-top control overlay whose points are sampled from the loaded model skeleton rest pose, with an optional model preview loaded from the pro...
- Uses one-finger drag in the 3D viewport to orbit the camera around the rig center, Blender-style.
- Uses two-finger drag in the 3D viewport to pan/zoom the rig view.
- Stores animation as portable pose channels: root, scale, and global humanoid 3D joint offsets.
- Defaults to stepped 12 fps pose playback.
- Supports keyframe add, duplicate, delete, mirror, previous/next key, playback, reset pose to the current model rest pose, reset 3D view, new clip creation, clip loading, model...
- Includes generated 12 fps JSON clips from the downloaded GLB walk/run files, sampled from GLB bone rotations into 3D joint positions.
- Supports bone selection mode on the 3D rig with highlighted selected bones.
- Stores authored edits as global humanoid `joint_offsets_3d` so clips can retarget across skeleton profiles with matching joint names.
- Drag inside the 3D viewport with one finger to orbit around the rig center.
- Double-tap or double-click a bone or visible control handle to enter selection mode.
- While selection mode is active, tap bones or handles to add/remove their driven bones from the selection. Selected bones turn yellow.
- Double-tap or double-click again on a selected rig element to exit selection mode while keeping the current selection highlighted. Double-tap empty space to clear the selection.
- When bones are selected, one finger still orbits the camera. Two-finger gestures edit the selection instead of the camera: center drag moves, pinch scales, two-finger pan in r...
- The control overlay includes hips, chest, head, hand IK, elbow pole, larger foot IK, foot-parented knee pole, heel, and toe handles. These controls are editor geometry, not im...
- Use Mirror to mirror selected left/right controls across the model centerline. If nothing side-specific is selected, Mirror applies to the available pose joints.
- Use New Clip to create an empty global retargetable 12 fps clip initialized from the current model rest pose.
- Use the model dropdown to switch skeleton profiles. Current global clips retarget through matching joint names, and the model preview reloads from the selected profile.
- Use the clip dropdown in the side panel to load blockout/imported clips.
- Use Model Preview to show/hide the loaded GLB scene behind the editable stick rig.
- Use Reset 3D to restore the rig rotation and camera framing.
- Timeline controls still operate at 12 fps with stepped pose playback.

Phalanx is a Godot 4.5 mobile-oriented prototype for authoring reusable, stepped 12 fps poses and clips on a rigged 3D character. The target workflow is closer to a lightweight ...
The current test asset is the Meshy/Ironhelm goblin biped in `assets/models/Meshy_AI_Ironhelm_Goblin_biped/` with its profile in `data/skeleton_profiles/ironhelm_biped.json`.
- `scripts/main.gd` owns app state, UI, keyframes, clip/profile loading, editing gestures, IK solving, and model-preview retargeting.
- `scripts/stick_rig_3d.gd` draws the editable always-on-top 3D stick rig and control overlay, handles picking, and converts pose dictionaries into joint positions.
- `tools/generate_imported_clips.py` samples GLB animation data into stepped 12 fps JSON clips under `data/clips/imported/`.
`scripts/stick_rig_2d.gd` still exists from the earlier 2D phase, but the app is currently 3D-only.
The visible editor rig is generated from the selected skeleton profile. It is not imported helper geometry from the GLB. The model preview is loaded separately from the profile ...
The app stores animation in portable pose data rather than model-specific transforms. Current authored edits use `joint_offsets_3d`, which are offsets from the profile rest join...
The default pose comes from the active profile/model rest pose. Resetting pose should return the model to its rest-pose control layout rather than a generic mannequin.
- `bone_map`: shared humanoid names to model `Skeleton3D` bone names
- `source_joints`: source skeleton bone names found in the GLB
- `display_joints_3d`: rest positions for the editor/control rig
- `display_bones_3d`: ordered parent-child joint pairs used to draw and edit bones
- legacy 2D fields such as `display_bones`, which should not drive new 3D work
A clip is a JSON object with fields like:
- `joint_offsets_3d`: retargetable per-joint offsets from profile rest pose.
- `joint_positions_3d`: legacy/imported absolute joint positions. These are accepted but should not be the final authored format.
- `foot_anchors_3d`: planted foot targets and toe offsets used by foot IK.
- `bone_rolls_3d`: per-bone long-axis roll values added by the roll gesture.
Saved local edits currently go to `data/clips/walk_blockout.local.json` unless the save path logic is changed.
The viewport intentionally follows a Blender-like split between camera and edit gestures:
- One-finger drag on empty/background space or while bones are selected orbits the 3D camera around the rig center.
- Two-finger gestures never rotate the camera. They pan/zoom the camera when no edit selection is active, and edit the active selection when bones are selected.
- Double tap/click a bone or visible control to enter selection mode.
- Single taps while in selection mode add/remove bones from the current selection.
- Double tap/click again on a selected rig element exits selection mode while keeping the selection highlighted.
- Translate: two-finger pan moves the selected control/bone set in the camera plane.
- Rotate: two-finger pan rotates selected FK bones in camera-facing axes. For IK/default-translate controls, rotate mode is reached by cycling modes.
- Longwise roll: in rotate mode, two-finger twist with little center movement rolls selected FK bones around their own long axis. The thresholds live in `EDIT_ROLL_DEADZONE` and...
- Scale: pinch scales the selected bone and descendants around the selected bone head/pivot.

Leg IK is handled in `scripts/main.gd`, mainly around `_solve_leg_to_foot`, `_apply_planted_feet`, and foot-control gesture helpers.
- Foot IK handles represent planted foot targets/anchors, not just the current solved foot joint.
- Knee pole controls are parented to the foot IK control so they follow foot target translation and height.
- If stretch is disabled, the foot target/anchor still stays planted; the mesh/solved chain should reach as well as it can without changing the anchor.
- Stretch toggles are per-limb and keyframeable in `limb_stretch`.
